about: Laundry Room Viking is a photo of a young man in glasses, a blue T-shirt and a horned Viking helmet, sitting in a plastic tub and paddling with a broom handle through a basement laundry room flooded with brown water up to the washer and dryer. His gritted-teeth expression sells it: he is treating a miserable chore like a seafaring raid. The meme borrows the sarcastic "they said" pattern, quoting someone's cheerful promise about a task and then letting the drowned basement show how it actually went.
origin: The photo was taken after Hurricane Irene flooded parts of the US East Coast in late August 2011. It circulated first as a Facebook profile picture, and the sarcastic "do the laundry" captions spread on Reddit within weeks.
usage:
Both boxes usually follow the "they said" structure. The top line quotes the advice or promise ("buy a house they said"), and the bottom line adds the second rosy claim ("it'll be relaxing they said"). The picture underneath is the rebuttal, so you don't need to spell out the disaster.

It works best for tasks that sounded easy or glamorous and turned into a slog: home ownership, group projects, adopting a puppy, moving apartments, a "quick" software update. Keep both lines parallel in rhythm so the repetition reads like a sigh.
ideas: it will build equity they said
take the group project they said
it'll be easy marks they said
it takes two minutes they said
go to the beach on a holiday they said
pick a starter Pokemon they said
